name: Albanian Macrolanguage

formality.description: Albanian has a T-V distinction: ti (singular informal) vs. ju (plural/formal). Formal address uses second-person plural verb forms with singular reference. Honorific titles (Zotëri, Zonja) are used in formal contexts. The T-V system is actively used in all Albanian-speaking regions.

gender.inclusiveGuidance: Albanian has a three-gender system: masculine, feminine, and neuter (neuter merges with masculine in plural). Gender triggers agreement on articles, adjectives, and pronouns. Albanian uses both preposed and postposed (suffixed) definite articles, with the suffixed article being the primary form.

linguisticChallenges.suffixedDefiniteArticle: Albanian suffixes the definite article to the noun: libër→libri 'the book', shtëpi→shtëpia 'the house'. The suffix varies by gender, number, and case. This is a Balkan sprachbund feature shared with Romanian and Bulgarian but not with most other Indo-European languages.
linguisticChallenges.balkanSprachbund: Albanian shares structural features with unrelated Balkan languages (Romanian, Bulgarian, Greek) due to centuries of contact: postposed definite article, loss of infinitive (replaced by subjunctive constructions with të), clitic doubling, and merged dative-genitive case.
linguisticChallenges.caseSystem: Albanian has five cases (nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, ablative) with distinct definite and indefinite declension paradigms. Adjectives also decline for case, gender, and definiteness.
linguisticChallenges.ghegToskDifferences: The two main Albanian varieties — Gheg (northern, spoken in Kosovo, northern Albania, North Macedonia) and Tosk (southern, basis of standard Albanian in Albania) — differ in phonology (Gheg has nasal vowels), some morphology (Gheg preserves infinitive), and vocabulary. Standard Albanian is based primarily on Tosk.
linguisticChallenges.admirativeAndEvidentiality: Albanian has a grammaticalized admirative mood (mënyra habitore) that expresses surprise, reported information, or non-firsthand evidence. This evidential/mirative category has no grammatical equivalent in most target languages and must be paraphrased.

notes: Macrolanguage card for Albanian (sqi). Covers Tosk Albanian (als, southern/standard) and Gheg Albanian (aln, northern/Kosovo). Both share Latin script, SVO order, M/F/N gender, suffixed definite articles, and Balkan sprachbund features. Albanian forms its own branch of Indo-European with no close relatives.

regions.region: Albania, Kosovo, North Macedonia (western), Montenegro, southern Serbia, diaspora in Greece/Italy
